dfx.example.goal: lenders for a $100M hotel financing in Atlanta

annotations.title: Which lenders have made commercial real estate loans like this one

description: Lenders ranked on the commercial real estate loans they ORIGINATED, from CMBS loan-level filings (SEC ABS-EE): same property type, loans in the states and city given, loans inside the size band nationally, recency and size fit. Each row names the lender (originator names normalised to the parent, a loan with several originators credits each), its local and national comparable counts and balances, the latest origination and three example loans with property, city, trust and the SEC filing. This is the answer to 'find lenders for a $100M hotel in Atlanta' or 'who lends on multifamily in Texas': use it, never find_lenders_for_financing, whose comparables are corporate BDC loans. A thin local market is carried by national comparables in the band and the envelope says how many were local. Conduit originators only: balance-sheet bank loans (most construction loans), debt funds and life companies are not on this tape, so pair it with search_bank_cre_exposure for local banks.

band_max_usd.description: The financing's own size, high end.

band_min_usd.description: The financing's own size, low end, for the size-fit factor.

city.description: The property's city, e.g. Atlanta. Counted within the states given.

property_type.description: The collateral. A hotel or resort is hotel.

since.description: ISO date; comparables originated on or after it. Default five years ago: conduit loans are 5 and 10 year paper, so five years of originations is the market active now.

size_max_usd.description: Largest comparable loan. Default twice band_max_usd, else no ceiling.

size_min_usd.description: Smallest comparable loan. Default half of band_min_usd, else no floor.

states.description: Two-letter states of the PROPERTY (not the lender), e.g. ["GA"].
